clues.text: Heavy and light accents are distinguished in tajwid, a set of rules for proper pronunciation while reciting this work.
A ritual based on this work uses the rules of tajweed, and can be performed without aid by a hafiz, someone who has memorized this text.
One of the most famous sections of this text is the Throne Verse, contained in its second and longest chapter.
The name of the first section of this work is translated as “The Opener” and is composed of seven ayats, or verses.
This work’s opening section, commonly used in salah, is nicknamed “the Key” and praises the “Sustainer of all worlds.”
This book may be divided into thirty juz' or seven manāzil, allowing it to be read in a month or a week.
This text is made up of 114 sections called suras.
Uthman standardized this text, including its “Cow” surah, which was received after the exile to Mecca by the prophet Muhammad.
This text is believed to be the word of God as passed down by the angel Gabriel to the prophet Muhammad.
Revealed by the angel Jibrīl over the course of twenty-three years to the prophet Muhammad, this is what central religious text of Islam?

answerlines: Baptism [accept Baptism of Jesus Christ; accept John the Baptist]

clues.text: The equivalent of this practice in Sikhism is called Amrit Sanchar or Khande di Pahul.
Alternate methods of undergoing this action can come “by blood” or “of desire,” according to Catholic doctrine.
The theologian Huldrich Zwingli believed that this practice was symbolic, and therefore not necessary.
Due to the wording of chapter 15, verse 29 of First Corinthians, Mormons perform this action on the dead.
This practice, which has alternative forms like aspersion and affusion, has controversially been performed on the dead by Mormons.
During one instance of this practice, the Holy Spirit descended in the form of a dove.
Many sects of Christianity developed from believing that doing this practice on infants meant nothing, because the infants don’t know if they believe in God, and are thus called “Ana-” this practice.
In certain denominations, a triple immersion is used to conduct this rite for infants, and holy water is sometimes used to remind people of this practice.
What Christian initiation ritual may involve sprinkling or pouring water on the subject’s head?
Name this admission rite of Christianity, which almost always involves water.

clues.text: One outgrowth of this religion was established by Vinitaruci and led to the founding of the Truc Lam and Lie Quán schools.
A text by one leader of this tradition asks, “if a mirror has no stand, where is the dust?.”
This tradition’s founder legendarily cut off his eyelids after falling asleep while staring at a wall for seven years.
One practitioner of this religion wrote a poem separating the comprehension of reality into five ranks.
The shakuhachi is an instrument which some adherents use to attain self-realization, and the Heart and Lotus aphorisms are recited in daily services at this religion's temples.
This religion claims that it originated from the Flower Sermon, and it was founded by the Chinese monk Bodhidharma.
It has its beginnings in the Flower Sermon, which started its spread throughout East Asia.
In the country in which it is most popular, it is divided into Soto and Rinzai sects that differ on how to achieve satori.
Adherents of this religion, which was practiced by Bodhidharma, attempt to reach satori, and it uses paradoxical koans for self-inquiry.
Name this tradition associated with Bodhidharma and known for its emphasis on meditation.
